newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha stable to higher, contango narrows.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha stable to higher, contango narrows.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were steady to a touch higher in thin afternoon trade on Tuesday, market participants said.
"Both buyers and sellers were hesitant in taking part in the market today, as overseas crude markets didn't show clear direction," one naphtha dealer said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half August, the only trading period in which traders showed actual buying interest, was bid at $199.50 per tonne against offers at $201.00.
First-half September was notionally assessed at $199.75/$201.25, compared with late Monday's $198.75/199.75.
The contango in inter-month naphtha spreads continued to narrow, with first-half September/first-half October discussed at minus 50 cents/plus 50 cents.
However, traders said there were no good reasons for the contraction in the contango.
"I think the contango should have been moving further apart, given the ample prompt supplies," one trader said.

In low sulphur fuel oil trading, a late July straight-run cargo was traded at $2.00 per barrel over the mean of Singapore quotes, traders said. Premiums for spot straight-run lots were quoted at about $1.70 to $1.80 last week. --Tokyo Energy Desk
